clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old lady presented with one month of abdominal pain, vomiting, and on examination, had epigastric/right hypochondriac tenderness and hepatomegaly. Initial imaging with Doppler ultrasound revealed no color flow in the hepatic veins. Grayscale ultrasound further showed heterogeneous liver echotexture, a fibrous cord replacing the middle hepatic vein, and mild ascites. A contrast-enhanced CT scan confirmed complete thrombosis of the middle and left hepatic veins, partial thrombosis of the right hepatic vein, slit-like visualization of the hepatic IVC, slight caudate lobe enlargement, and a heterogeneous mottled liver (nutmeg liver). Diagnostic hepatic vein venography subsequently confirmed these imaging findings, establishing the diagnosis of Budd Chiari syndrome.

CECT showed complete thrombosis of middle and left hepatic veins, partial thrombosis of the right hepatic vein, slit-like visualization of the hepatic IVC, slight enlargement of the caudate lobe, and heterogeneous mottled liver (nutmeg liver).
Diagnostic hepatic vein venography confirmed the imaging findings of venous obstruction.
